title: The world: ten stadiums on one continent, ten captains

status_vocabulary.accepted: Jack answered; the selected option and scope are recorded

brief: Jack, 2026-09-24: expand to 10 stadiums that make up a continent, each in the region that fits it (ice in a cold place, one in a volcano, one on a tropical island), selectable from the menu; define hazards, night lights and other defining features per stadium; grow to 10 captains, each assigned a field; one field is a tropical beach.

decisions.question: When does building start?

options.label: Plan now, build after #346
options.tradeoff: Nothing is built until Jack passes the Exhibition gate (#346). Safest for focus; the world waits.

options.label: Plan now; rails and greyboxes now; art after #346
options.tradeoff: The data rails, the new captains in data, the four new park files, new hazard patterns, greyboxes and the map picker are built now. No park art. Changes one AGENTS.md line: extra parks move from 'do not start' to 'greybox only'.

options.label: Build everything now
options.tradeoff: Parks and art become products now. Conflicts with AGENTS.md, #37 and FD-17.

decisions.existing_contract: AGENTS.md 'Do not start: extra parks as products (#37)'; FD-01 (rails and greyboxes allowed); FD-17 (greybox sitting before art).
decisions.acceptance: One scope line in AGENTS.md an agent can obey without asking.

decisions.question: In what order does park art come?

options.label: Keep FD-17
options.tradeoff: All ten as greyboxes first; Jack sits each greybox; then art one park at a time.

options.label: Art as each new park is built
options.tradeoff: Faster to look good; risks art on a park whose play is not settled.

decisions.existing_contract: FD-17 (greybox sitting before art, one park in art at a time).
decisions.acceptance: The art order written in the plan.

decisions.question: Do backdrops come back?

options.label: Blender kit art per park
options.tradeoff: The region past the fence is authored art (the volcano, the sea). Behind WD-02.

options.label: Data greybox backdrops now, art later
options.tradeoff: A backdrop row per region: a silhouette shape and a palette, drawn by one builder for every park. Reads as a place at greybox stage.

options.label: No backdrops
options.tradeoff: The field stays in an empty sky until art.

decisions.existing_contract: FD-16-R2 (the hand-built backdrops were deleted; identity returns only as art). B is a data rail, not per-park Unity art.
decisions.acceptance: A park's backdrop is named by its kit row and drawn by one builder; no park id in code.

decisions.question: Are the ten parks unlocked by play?

options.label: All ten open
options.tradeoff: Every park is on the map from the first boot.

options.label: Harbor and a few open; the rest unlock by play
options.tradeoff: A reason to play; needs a save file and an unlock rule.

options.label: All open in Exhibition; unlocks only in a later Challenge mode
options.tradeoff: Exhibition stays simple; unlocks wait for Challenge (#36).

decisions.existing_contract: #36 (Challenge after Exhibition is fun); research: 'unlock parks through play, not a shop'.
decisions.acceptance: The map shows which parks are open and why.

decisions.question: What is the continent's shape and name?

options.label: The draft
options.tradeoff: The Diamond Isles: a main continent with the cold north, jungle west, city east and warm south, plus one tropical island off the south coast.

options.label: Jack's own layout
options.tradeoff: Jack names the shape, the name and where each park sits.

decisions.acceptance: A named continent and a map position for every park.

decisions.question: Which ten parks?

options.label: The draft ten
options.tradeoff: The six parks in data, plus Stillwater Marsh, Coconut Cove, Sunscorch Mesa and Summit Park.

options.label: Swap in a deferred park
options.tradeoff: Haunt Manor, Cruise Deck or Playroom replaces one of Stillwater Marsh, Sunscorch Mesa or Summit Park.

decisions.recommendation: A: every region looks different, and a desert and a mountain are new for the genre. Haunt Manor needs a hazard pattern the library does not have (input disruption, FD-09).
decisions.existing_contract: docs/parks.md (Haunt Manor, Cruise Deck, Playroom deferred, #37).

decisions.question: Where does Elder Fenn play at home?

options.label: Stillwater Marsh
options.tradeoff: Fenn gets a park of their own; one captain, one field.

options.label: Fenn keeps sharing Harbor
options.tradeoff: The tenth park goes to a fourth new captain.

decisions.existing_contract: Parks: 'faction' is unique per park; Stillwater has no park today.
decisions.acceptance: Every captain names exactly one home park.

decisions.question: How many hazards does a park have?

options.label: One primary hazard plus one night change
options.tradeoff: The parks.md rule. Each park has one thing to learn by day and one thing that changes at night.

options.label: Two hazards per park
options.tradeoff: More variety; harder to read at gameplay distance and to teach.

decisions.existing_contract: docs/parks.md 'One park, one primary gimmick'; research: one primary gimmick and a night variant.
decisions.acceptance: Each park sheet names one day hazard and one night change.

decisions.question: Which new hazard patterns are built?

options.label: All three, one child each
options.tradeoff: Surge (the tide), drifting redirect (dust devils), fog bank (Stillwater). Each is a closed-library row with its own tests; none awards a result (FD-08).

options.label: Only what the existing patterns can do
options.tradeoff: The new parks reuse status volumes, redirects, solid bodies and timed movers.

options.label: A and B mixed
options.tradeoff: Build surge and drifting redirect; give Stillwater an existing pattern instead of fog.

decisions.recommendation: C. Fog as a vision effect hides the ball from a human and not from the CPU (FD-14: the CPU reads the park), which is unfair. Stillwater's hazard becomes floating lily pads (solid bodies on a timed drift) unless Jack wants fog as look only.
decisions.existing_contract: FD-08 (a hazard may be random, never decides a result); FD-09 (closed pattern library); FD-14 (CPU reads the park); FD-19 (off the base paths).
decisions.acceptance: Every new type has a row naming its pattern; a scenario per pattern shows the ball and bodies still decide the play.

decisions.question: What are night lights?

options.label: A themed light rig per park, plus its night look
options.tradeoff: Towers, torches, neon or lanterns as kit art; the sky and light rows in looks.json. The play light stays the same.

options.label: Night look rows only
options.tradeoff: No light props; only the sky and light change.

options.label: Night also changes the light you play in
options.tradeoff: For example a darker outfield. Reopens FD-11-R2.

decisions.recommendation: A. The rig is a kit slot (the 'night' slot) filled per park, greybox first (a data row: pole count, height, lamp color).
decisions.existing_contract: FD-11-R2 (lights stay on; night changes only the view outside and the hazards).
decisions.acceptance: Every park names a night rig; the field is lit the same at every park.

decisions.question: Who are the three new captains?

options.label: The draft
options.tradeoff: Kai (beach, Tide Riders), Sable (desert, Dune Nomads), Hollis (mountain, Peak Guard).

options.label: Jack's own
options.tradeoff: Jack names them, or changes any one.

decisions.recommendation: A. The beach captain was renamed from the first draft on Jack's request (no name close to a Nintendo name).
decisions.acceptance: Three names, colors and identity lines.

decisions.question: Do the new captains found new factions?

options.label: Yes, one new faction each
options.tradeoff: Ten factions, one captain and one park each; chemistry gets three new groups to learn.

options.label: They join existing factions
options.tradeoff: Fewer factions; a faction has two parks, which the unique-faction rule refuses today.

decisions.existing_contract: docs/roster.md 'one captain per faction'; the park 'faction' field is unique.
decisions.acceptance: Ten factions, each with one captain and one home park.

decisions.question: When do the new factions get role players?

options.label: Now: three each, like the others
options.tradeoff: Nine new role players with stats and chemistry.

options.label: Captains first, role players later
options.tradeoff: A new faction fields its captain and borrows role players until its own exist.

decisions.recommendation: B: keeps one rig and one art queue (AGENTS.md); #687 keeps extras off until they read as toys.
decisions.acceptance: The lineup fills a nine for every captain.

decisions.question: What body class does each new captain have?

options.label: A new class row each
options.tradeoff: The class table has room for about fifteen rows (CH-11); a new captain gets its own size, weight and motion style.

options.label: Reuse an existing class
options.tradeoff: Faster; the new captains read less distinct.

decisions.recommendation: A, after CF-3 (#1116) lands the class table.
decisions.existing_contract: CH-05, CH-11, CH-12 (body classes are data; about fifteen rows); CF-3 #1116.
decisions.acceptance: Every captain resolves exactly one class (SC-09).

decisions.question: Do the new captains bring new star abilities?

options.label: New abilities
options.tradeoff: Each captain gets a star pitch, a star swing and a field ability of its own. Each is gameplay work with a lesson.

options.label: Reuse the ability library
options.tradeoff: The new captains draw from the abilities that exist; their identity is stats, body and park.

options.label: One new ability each, the rest reused

decisions.recommendation: C: one signature ability each (the draft names them), the rest from the library.
decisions.existing_contract: #1011 (Phase 6 replacement effects open); tutorials contract (every mechanic has a lesson).
decisions.acceptance: Every ability a captain names exists in data/abilities and has a lesson.

decisions.question: Does the home park give an edge?

options.label: Cosmetic
options.tradeoff: Home park is only where a faction's captain plays at home.

options.label: A small home edge
options.tradeoff: For example a crowd boost to the Star meter at home.

decisions.question: How is the stadium picked?

options.label: A continent map with park pins
options.tradeoff: The stick moves between pins; each pin shows the postcard, crest, hazard line and night rig; South confirms.

options.label: The left/right cycle plus a map postcard
options.tradeoff: Today's row, with a small map showing where the park is.

options.label: Both
options.tradeoff: Map in Exhibition setup, cycle in a quick rematch.

decisions.existing_contract: docs/how-to-play.md stadium row; HowToPlay.cs; one screen for one and two pads.
decisions.acceptance: Both pads can pick any park; how-to-play and HowToPlay.cs change in the same PR.

decisions.question: What does the map look like?

options.label: A painted 2-D map (art slot)
options.tradeoff: One illustrated map image in an art slot, with pins drawn over it.

options.label: A 3-D diorama
options.tradeoff: The continent as a small 3-D model the camera flies over. More work; more toy.

options.label: Greybox first, then A or B
options.tradeoff: A flat shape map from the region data now; art later.

decisions.existing_contract: Catalog first, files second (AGENTS.md): a map slot + validator + empty folder, then the art.
decisions.acceptance: The map draws from region data with no art present.

history.quote: let's plan on expanding to 10 stadiums that make up a contentent where you can select the one you play on the menu
pick a new name instead of mario. but otherwise i like it. let's create a matrix to track all these decisions and expand on details.
history.effect: The beach captain's draft name changed to Kai. Feedback on the draft as a whole; no decision is recorded as accepted from it. This register and the expanded plan were written.
